findings.ac: Status: a failing log fetch keeps the PR red and big
findings.text: _failing_detail() calls _gh('run','view',...,'--log-failed') with no try/except; a GhError there propagates out of gate_status() into cmd_status, which emits verdict 'none' exit 0 (a false pass) instead of red+big. No test covers a failing log fetch (FakeGh.logs KeyError is never exercised as a gh failure).

findings.ac: Status: a gh failure after the first read is pending
findings.text: cmd_status maps every GhError (first read or later poll) to verdict 'none' exit 0 with reason 'gh unavailable'. There is no first-read vs later-read distinction, so a mid-poll gh failure never yields 'pending'; no test exercises a gh failure after the first pr view.

findings.ac: Status: missing gh is none (exit 0), unusable gh is cannot_run (exit 2)
findings.text: _gh()/cmd_status never emit verdict 'cannot_run' or exit 2 for status: OSError (missing) and non-zero exit (unusable, e.g. unauthenticated) both become none/exit 0. test_status_gh_unavailable_is_none_exit_0 only covers the missing case; the unusable -> cannot_run/exit 2 path is neither implemented nor tested.

findings.ac: Fix path and wiring: exit 2 halts [CI-RED] could not check
findings.text: Neither src/references/ci-gate.md section 4, 4a step 7/8, nor 3z Step 3A mention status exit 2 / cannot_run or the '[CI-RED] could not check' halt, and test_ci_gate_wiring.py has no assertion for that string. Only the parity halt '[CI-PARITY] could not run' exists.

findings.ac: Classifier: big for a parsed failure in an untouched file whatever the job is named
findings.text: classify() applies the MECHANICAL regex to f'{check} {step} {log_tail}', so a pytest/jest failure in an untouched file in a job or step named e.g. 'lint', 'format' or 'eslint' (or whose log contains those words) is skipped as mechanical and returns small. The spec says a parsed test failure is never mechanical and the name must not matter; test_classify_big only uses check 'test'/'Run tests' and never tests a lint-named job with an untouched parsed failure.

findings.ac: Scope change: pre-push parity dropped (Overview, Notes 'Not building a pre-push local CI replay')
findings.text: The issue states parity was built, measured and dropped before ship, but the snapshot still ships ci_gate.py parity (cmd_parity, select_steps, find_bash), a 4a step 4 parity halt ([CI-PARITY], parity:waived), 3z [CI-PARITY] handling, reference section 1, and the fix-order test requiring `parity` before push. Code/docs contradict the stated spec and ACs (which name only status/classifier/cap).

findings.ac: Time-to-Value: one blocking call run with the host's maximum tool timeout
findings.text: Default 480 s cap and no-run-when-no-checks (verdict none) are tested, but no workflow/reference text instructs running ci_gate.py status with the host's maximum tool timeout (no 'timeout' text in ci-gate.md, 4a step 8 or 3z Step 3A) and no wiring test asserts it.

The gate fixture stubs _base_is_stale to False and no test asserts result['base_stale'] is True in status output or that _base_is_stale/merge-base logic works; only classify() with stale=True is covered.
